interpretation: This is broader actual TRAIN fit, not heldout generalization or profitability. The paired models share1024 entries, native epoch1 samples, frozen teacher91 and eval mode. No replay training was performed.

Both Exit HOLD MSE values increased on this measured cohort after2385 real optimizer steps. LONG remains slightly worse than zero; SHORT is slightly better than zero but worse than before95. This is descriptive, not a statistical significance or sole-cause claim.
Forecast MSE improved at25/60/120minutes while action learning did not. Constant trading or complete disconnection of all features is not supported.

Entry value targets are effectively immediate first-M1 liquidation on1021/1024 entries; teacher continuation changes only3 entries fromFLAT totrade. Earlier64-entry decomposition is reused as supporting evidence, not treated as a new finding.

One-step bootstrap plus teacher refresh only after full epoch/VAL is a concrete credit-assignment hypothesis; these observations do not prove that changing cadence or multi-step backup will fix learning.

The v4 reward already includes the v3 liquidation-value adjustment. Relative reward reduces to executable value change plus physical carrying cost. Do not falsely treat it as unadjusted potential shaping or repeat the old terminal-cash HOLD diagnosis.

next_bounded_change_proposal.hypothesis: A frozen-policy multi-step backup can carry observed later value into Exit and hence Entry sooner than the current one-M1 backup.
next_bounded_change_proposal.scope: Existing model/economics/sampler owners only. Five observed M1 successor transitions align the existing M5 Entry data cadence; this is a learning-backup extent, never a maximum holding time or policy EXIT rule.

Use wall-clock discount and declared market closures; keep original sampled states and loss weights.
Keep all features/families/timeframes, forecast supervision, task weighting, gradient boundaries, model structure and EMA unchanged.
